correctness.rationale: For x_n=cq^n in (0,2), normalized Szegő Gram G decomposes as G=H∘R=D(H+H∘J)D with H_nm=sech((n−m)|log q|/2), J_nm=1/(u_n+u_m), u_n=1/x_n−1/2>0, d_n=sqrt(1−x_n/2). R is a positive normalized Gram correlation (diagonal 1), so the unital Schur map transfers both optimal Toeplitz bounds. J and D−I are trace class, establishing G−H trace class and identical essential spectra. DLMF dn Fourier/θ identities give symbol range [theta4(sqrt q)^2,theta3(sqrt q)^2]; translated long plane waves put this full range into essential spectrum. No spectral outliers can lie outside transferred bounds. Independently checked Gram factorization, PSD and endpoint inequalities for three q,c,N settings and Fourier sums.

originality.rationale: The theta endpoint identity itself and standard Toeplitz essential spectra are classical and excluded. Baranov–Batenev construct representing systems of Szegő kernels using different configurations, not the exact global Gram spectrum of one geometric radial chain. Pushnitski studies homogeneous integer-index Hardy kernel matrices, where outliers can occur; his theorem does not imply no outliers here. A prior interpolation/Riesz inequality under a different operator formulation remains possible.

Trace-class equivalence does not classify embedded spectrum or spectral type.

value.rationale: The exact best Riesz constants and entire spectrum for a canonical radial interpolating Blaschke sequence give a genuine structural result. Mere compact Toeplitz comparison would allow isolated eigenvalues; the normalized positive Schur factor is the essential new mechanism excluding them uniformly for all starting c. It provides precise condition numbers for stable interpolation on the closed span.
